imagery_note.value: No optical satellite scene was classified or interpreted in this project, so capture date and sun angle do not apply. Satellite-derived products were used ready-made and are named for what they are: GPM IMERG rain (passive-microwave and infrared estimates merged by NASA; the value of a day is the UTC day), the elevation tiles (a composite tile set in SRTM format: its main source, the SRTM radar mission of February 2000, is an active sensor, and the tiles do not say which source a cell came from), and the Annual NLCD land-cover map of 2011 (made by USGS from Landsat images; the map year is the date that applies). The weather tables (Daymet, NLDAS, MERRA-2, ERA5, AORC, Stage IV, GEFS) are gauge analyses, radar-and-gauge analyses, model reanalyses or forecasts: not images.

caption_basin_maps.value: Elevation inside each basin outline, one row per landscape, basins ordered by size. Colours are stretched PER BASIN: light = the lowest point of that basin, dark = its highest point, and the range in metres is printed above each map. This shows the valleys of the flat Florida basins (a few tens of metres of relief) as clearly as those of the Appalachian basins (more than 1,000 m), but a colour does NOT mean the same height in two panels. Relief shading (light from the north-west) is added for texture; in low-relief basins it is exaggerated (factor 400 m / the basin's elevation range between its 2nd and 98th percentile, at most 12, on a smoothed grid), so shading strength must not be compared between panels either. North is up in every map; each panel has its own km scale bar; the white dot is the river gauge.

One cubic foot is 0.0283168 cubic metres and a day has 86,400 seconds, so cfs x 0.0283168 x 86,400 is the volume that passed the gauge in the day, in cubic metres; dividing by the basin area in square metres gives metres of water over the basin, and x 1000 gives millimetres. Rain and flow are then in the same unit.

words_basin_mean_with_overlap_weights.value: A grid cell lies wholly or partly inside a basin. IMERG (0.1 degree) and GEFS (0.25 degree) cells are large against the basins, so every cell that overlaps the outline counts in proportion to the area of the overlap. For AORC (1/120 degree) and Stage IV (4.76 km) the cells are small, so the basin mean is the plain mean of the cells whose centre lies inside the outline (their areas differ by under 1% within a basin).

formula_local_day_sum.value: R_t = sum of the hourly rain r_h over the hours h whose end lies in (00:00, 24:00] of local day t
formula_local_day_sum.text: R_t = sum of the hourly rain r_h over the hours h whose end lies in (00:00, 24:00] of local day t

words_local_day_sum.value: A forecast is issued at local midnight at the end of day t, and hourly rain is stamped in UTC by the end of the hour. Every hour is given to the local calendar day in which it ends, by the gauge's wall clock (zoneinfo: America/New_York for 11 basins, America/Chicago for Leaf River; summer time included), and the hours of a day are summed. A day has 24 hours, or 23 or 25 where the clocks change (34 days of 23 hours and 34 days of 25 hours in the 34 years). No hour after the issue time is summed: proved for every hour by the wall clock, in UTC time, by a second route from the time-zone rules, and by replacing the later hours with made-up values (15_rain_to_midnight.py, 16_aorc_rain_to_midnight.py).

words_scaled_inputs.value: Each column is put on one scale with the mean and standard deviation of the training years (1980-10-01 to 2000-09-30), pooled over the training basins; the flow enters as log(1 + q_mm); the 10 basin properties are scaled over the training basins. The values are fitted on the training years only, so nothing of the validation or test years leaks into the scale (recomputed here and equal to the scalers stored in a saved network).

formula_high_flow_level_and_onset.value: level_b = quantile_0.95(q_mm of basin b over the training years); high day: q > level_b; onset at lead k: q(t+k) > level_b and q(t) <= level_b

words_high_flow_level_and_onset.value: A basin's high-flow level is the 95th percentile of its daily flow in the training years: a day above it is a high-flow day. A warning is given when the forecast exceeds the level (times a warning level chosen on the validation years). An onset is a high-flow day whose forecast was issued while the river was still at or below the level; 1 day ahead that is exactly the first day of each event (consecutive high-flow days). The 12 basins have 611 onsets in the test years. The share of onsets warned is the main score.

formula_training_loss_and_stopping.value: loss = mean over scored days of w_b x (forecast_scaled - flow_scaled)^2, w_b = 1 / (sd_b / sd_all + 0.1)^2

words_training_loss_and_stopping.value: The loss is the squared error of the scaled flow, weighted so that wet and dry basins count nearly alike (the weight is about 1 over the basin's flow variance in the training years). Every 100 updates the model is scored on the validation years of the same basins (mean NSE over basins and leads); the best state is kept and training stops after 6 checks without a gain or at 2,000 updates.

words_gefs_bias_factor_and_issue_time.value: The run used is the 00 UTC run of the UTC date t+1 (init_date = t+1): 4 h old at the Eastern issue time in summer, 5 h in winter, 5 or 6 h at the Central one (the latest 00 UTC run that exists at the issue time; the run of the date t+2 starts after it). The days: local day t+k = the wall-clock day of the gauge (zoneinfo America/New_York, America/Chicago for Leaf River, summer time included), forecast hours (lo, hi] of the run with lo = local midnight that starts the day, hi = the one that ends it, counted from the run's start; the amounts of the 3-hourly windows inside the day are summed, a window that straddles a boundary is split in proportion to the time inside (1/3 or 2/3, uniform rain inside a window assumed). The bias factor: bias factor per basin and lead = (sum of the AORC rain of the local days t+k) / (sum of the forecast rain of the same days) over the issue days whose TARGET day t+k lies in the validation years 2000-10-01 .. 2005-09-30 (flood.SPLIT['val']); fc_bc = fc_raw x factor, for every day of 2000-2014 (a factor fitted on the validation years only, applied unchanged to the test years); a single factor per basin and lead: no seasonal correction.

training_curves_caption.value: Learning curves of three training set-ups of the LSTM. Top: training loss. Bottom: NSE in the validation years, mean of 1 to 3 days ahead (left: of the one river; middle and right: mean of the 12 rivers); dot and band: the state that was kept. Left column: the base setting of the tuning, one training (its other 2 seeds were kept at updates 125 and 50; curves not stored), not the chosen setting (16 memory cells, learning rate 0.005, 30 days of history). Right column: with the perfect weather forecast, an upper bound that cannot be had in practice. Each column has its own scales. Updates are not passes through the data: 50 on one river go through its training years about 80 times, as 600 do on 12 rivers. What to see: on the left the blue line falls after update 50 while the grey line falls further (overfitting); in the middle and on the right the blue lines peak at updates 500 to 800 and at updates 800 to 1,300.

kf_headline.value: Among the models tried, the limit is the information in the inputs, not the network: 1 day ahead, on the same inputs (past weather + river gauge) four kinds of model lie within 0.03 NSE and 8 percentage points of onsets warned of each other, while rain up to the evening of the issue day lifts the LSTM's onsets warned from 19% to 30% (about a quarter of the gap; in NSE the result is mixed) and rain up to midnight from a radar- and gauge-anchored analysis (AORC, an analysis made after the fact) lifts them from 19% to 52% (48% with the real-time radar product Stage IV in its place); 2 and 3 days ahead a real weather forecast (GEFS) lifts them from 8% and 6% to 38% and 37% (in NSE the gain is mixed); a perfect weather forecast, an upper bound that cannot be had in practice, would give 64% 1 day ahead and 67% and 68% 2 and 3 days ahead; for onsets the verdict is still NOT YET for every set that could be had in practice.

e1_outcome_caveat.value: The NLDAS rain up to the evening gives a higher share (30%, 183 hits of 611) than the rain to midnight (29%, 180 hits of 611); the five single trainings with the rain to midnight span 27.5% to 31.6%; the control is not flat (21% against 19% with the rain table alone); the success rule of the work order (clearly above the NLDAS result in every training, control flat) is not met. The control with the same rain over the table's own window is flat (20.3% against 18.7% with the rain table alone), so the gain of 9.2 points comes from the hours after about 09:00 (76 onsets warned only by the rain to midnight against 20 only by that control). Ridge regression and the random forest given the same input warn of 26.8% and 27.0% (the new input adds 16.2 and 8.8 points to them, 10.8 to the LSTM), so the gain does not need the network.

Nothing else changed: the same settings (results/lstm_all.json, key config), inputs, split, stopping rule, warning level and success rule. Every seed average (lstm_<set>.npz) and every seed range of this script now covers five trainings; the control sets of 04_lstm_all.py and 10_rain_timing.py keep their three. The two extra seeds were planned on 14 October 2026 (code/schedule.py, week 2: five trainings per model where the NSE decides; promised at the proposal talk of 15 October) for every set alike, whatever the direction of its result; the three-seed numbers remain in the independent review records (the rounds of results/review_rain_to_midnight.json made before 30 October) and in a copy of the three-seed results file, results/archive/rain_to_midnight_3seeds_2026-10-30.json (copied unchanged from the backup of 30 October 2026, 10:41); passes records only the trainings and times of each pass. five_seed_changes lists what changed with five seeds. With five seeds instead of three (the three-seed results file is kept unchanged as results/archive/rain_to_midnight_3seeds_2026-10-30.json) these numbers and words changed, the three-seed values in brackets. Lead 1, test years: lstm_wqh onsets warned 29.5% (30.0%; 180 hits against 183), median NSE 0.663 (0.657); lstm_wqh_older onsets warned 20.9% (21.4%; 128 hits against 131), median NSE 0.616 (0.618); lstm_wh onsets warned 31.3% (31.9%; 191 hits against 195), median NSE 0.508 (0.503); lstm_wh_older onsets warned 18.0% (19.5%; 110 hits against 119), median NSE 0.463 (0.450); lstm_wqh_to09 onsets warned 20.3% (20.5%; 124 hits against 125), median NSE 0.538 (0.579); lstm_wqh_utc onsets warned 22.6% (21.8%; 138 hits against 133), median NSE 0.620 (0.593); lstm_wqnh onsets warned 32.4% (31.8%; 198 hits against 194), median NSE 0.694 (0.687). e1b_outcome_caveat.value: The ERA5 rain to midnight of script 15 gives a lower share (29%, 180 hits of 611) than the AORC rain to midnight (52%, 316 hits of 611); the NLDAS rain up to the evening gives a lower share (30%, 183 hits of 611) than the AORC rain to midnight (52%, 316 hits of 611); the five single trainings with the AORC rain to midnight span 48.6% to 55.3%; the success rule of the work order (clearly above the NLDAS result in every training, control flat) is met. The control with the same AORC rain over the table's own window is flat (18.0% against 18.7% with the rain table alone), so the gain of 33.7 points over that control (33.1 points over the rain table alone) comes from the hours after about 09:00 (228 onsets warned only by the AORC rain to midnight against 22 only by that control). Against the ERA5 rain to midnight over the same hours the AORC rain warns of +22.3 points (316 against 180 hits of 611; every training with AORC above every training with ERA5: yes), so the E1 gain grows with it (step 1b of the roadmap). Ridge regression and the random forest given the same input warn of 55.2% and 48.0% (the new input adds 44.5 and 29.8 points to them, 33.1 to the LSTM), so the gain does not need the network. On the median NSE the LSTM (0.76) against ridge regression (0.64) and the random forest (0.66): report section 4.2 reads 'the LSTM is ahead' for ridge regression and 'the LSTM is ahead' for the forest; on the onsets, the headline, ridge regression warns of more (55.2% against 51.7%, 67% of its warnings false against 51%; 1 of the 5 LSTM trainings is above it); the random forest warns of fewer (48.0% against 51.7%, 53% of its warnings false against 51%; 5 of the 5 LSTM trainings are above it). With the AORC rain in the place of the Daymet rain column (no extra column) the LSTM warns of 53% of the onsets against 19% with the Daymet rain table (44.8% to 54.8% against 18.0% to 18.5% in the single trainings; +33.9 points over the rain table alone, more in every training), but that comparison changes the product (Daymet to AORC) and the clock (a day that ends at about 09:00 to one that ends at midnight) together and is not a verdict on the Daymet product: the same AORC rain over the table's own window adds -0.7 points to the rain table alone, over the whole day it adds +33.7 points to that control, the replaced table adds +33.9 points to the rain table alone, and against AORC as an extra column it adds +0.8 points (no clear difference); the data support that the hours after about 09:00 are worth about 34 points (the two gains above, averaged), and whether the Daymet product itself costs skill apart from its clock was not isolated (AORC over 09:00 to 09:00 in the place of the Daymet column was not run). AORC is a retrospective analysis, not rain that could be read at midnight: its hours are daily totals on a gauge day that ends at 12 UTC, spread over the hours with radar and corrected about 10 days behind real time, and the hours before 2002, which are all the training years, are disaggregated daily totals. An independent review (results/review_aorc_rain_to_midnight.json) tested what that could do to the test years: on 78 days (936 basin-days) the AORC rain before local midnight does not depend on the Stage IV rain after it (coefficient -0.030 mm per mm, 95% interval -0.060 to -0.001), and with Stage IV, a real-time product (about one hour behind), in place of AORC on the issue day the three networks of seeds 0-2 that the review tested warn of 86 to 95 of the 171 onsets of those days against 92 with AORC (the rain table alone: 15), that is 92% to 104% of the AORC effect; a hindsight that the review could not exclude would cost those networks at most about 3 points of their 51% (16 of 313 hits); the other 440 onsets were not tested by the review; with all five networks, Stage IV in place of AORC on the issue day costs 22 of 316 hits on all 611 onsets (3.6 points; 5 hits, 0.8 points, with the level of AORC restored). Stage IV in place of AORC on the issue day of all 611 onsets (results/stage4_realtime.json): 294 of 611 warned against 316 with AORC and 114 with the rain table alone, 89% of the AORC effect survives (95% interval 83% to 95%, drawing issue days); with the last hour of the issue day taken out, as the delay of Stage IV would, 276 are warned (80% of the effect) and with the level of AORC restored (Stage IV times 1.06) 311. That count is driven by heavy rain on the issue day more than by its exact amount: with the Stage IV rain of another onset day of the same basin in its place 286 onsets are warned, with the AORC rain of an ordinary day 36, with no rain 13; the mean absolute error of the forecast on the onset days, which does depend on the exact rain, is 4.64 mm/day with Stage IV, 4.62 with AORC and 5.64 with another onset's rain.

s4_outcome.value: With Stage IV rain (radar and gauge, the product a service at midnight would read) in place of AORC on the issue day of each of the 611 onsets, the five saved lstm_wqa networks warn of 294 (48%) against 316 with AORC (52%) and 114 with the rain table alone (19%): 89% of the AORC effect survives (95% interval 83% to 96% drawing onsets, 83% to 95% drawing issue days). With the level of AORC restored (Stage IV times 1.06) 311 are warned; with the last hour of the issue day taken out 276, with the last two hours 257. On the issue days of all 12 basins (the warnings issued when the river was low; Stage IV in every basin on those days) Stage IV gives 292 hits and 98 false warnings (25% of the warnings) against 316 hits and 132 false warnings (29%) with AORC, and with the level of AORC restored 310 and 116 (27%). The count is more sensitive to whether the issue day was a heavy-rain day than to its exact rain: with the Stage IV rain of another onset of the same basin in its place the networks still warn of 286 (279 to 295 in 10 draws), with the AORC rain of an ordinary day 36, with no rain 13. The mean absolute error of the forecast on the onset days, which does depend on the exact rain, is 4.62 mm/day with AORC, 4.64 with Stage IV, 5.64 with another onset's Stage IV rain, 6.66 with an ordinary day's rain and 5.83 with the rain table alone.

review_e1b_verdict.value: E1b holds up under independent recomputation, and the hindsight risk I was asked to test hard does not show up in the test years. Every number I could recompute equals the builder's (313 of 611 onsets = 51.2%, single trainings 48.6, 48.6 and 55.3%; controls 17.7, 37.5 and 18.7%; ERA5 30.0%; ridge 55.2%, forest 48.0%; replaced table 51.6%; median NSE 0.767 against 0.590; over 3,000 derived values; the 12 saved networks bit for bit from tables I built myself; the figure to 0.2 point), no hour after a window's end enters any input (90 perturbation cases), the AORC series equals my own reduction of the raw chunks (0.00 mm; 408 filled and 264 partial hours re-read from the raw files), and the engine files changed by another agent are additive and pass their test. On hindsight: the documentation shows that the channel exists by construction (daily totals on a 12 UTC gauge day spread over the hours by Stage IV's hourly shape, so an hour before midnight can carry a factor set by a day that includes rain after the issue time), but on 78 test-year days (the builder's 50 plus 28 I chose by onsets and night storms, which hold 11.8 mm of Stage IV rain after midnight on average against 1.1 mm in the builder's) the AORC rain before midnight does not depend on the Stage IV rain after it (coefficient -0.030, 95% -0.060 to -0.001; 35 dry-before/wet-after basin-days hold 0.08 mm before midnight), and the saved networks given Stage IV, a real-time product, in place of AORC for the issue day warn of 86 to 95 of the 171 onsets of those days against 92 with AORC (the rain table alone: 15). Best estimate of the part of the 51% that could be hindsight: none; at most about 3 points, measured on 28% of the onsets, not proven for the other 440 (about 10-13 GB of Stage IV would cover them). What needs fixing is wording and records, not numbers: the last clause of outcome_full ('the mis-stamped table itself costs skill') is not supported as worded, and the sentence that documents must quote says nothing about AORC being a retrospective analysis; the other items (the NSE-only reading of 'the LSTM is clearly ahead', leads 2-3, the by-period reading, the 88 GB, the log, the reproduction path, the registry announcement) are in should_fix. The 51% is a good measurement of what well-measured rain up to midnight is worth; it is not an operational warning (verdict NOT YET), and its transfer to a real-time service rests on the 171 onsets I could test with Stage IV, not yet on all 611.

review_e1b_trust.value: As a measurement: fully. 313 of 611 onsets (51.2%) is exactly what the saved networks give, every number, clock, network and derived field reproduces, nothing after the issue time enters the input, and the one risk that could have made it an artefact (hindsight in AORC's daily anchoring) is not there to the extent I can measure it: best estimate 0 points, at most about 3. As a statement about what the information is worth: 51% is what rain up to midnight is worth when it is known as well as AORC knows it (a retrospective analysis, 10-day production lag, hours before 2002 disaggregated); with Stage IV, a real-time product, in AORC's place the same networks keep 86-95 of their 92 warnings on the 171 onsets of the stormiest days I could test (28% of all onsets: 50-56% of those onsets against 54% with AORC), so a real-time version should land close to the same share, at most about 3 points lower; the delay of the last radar hour (about 1 hour behind) is not counted. Its size: a share of 611 onsets has a binomial standard error of 2.0 points (more with storm clustering: 3.5 and 2.5 points in the two halves of the test years), three trainings span 48.6-55.3%, so quote it as 51% with the seed range 48.6-55.3% and a standard error of about 2-3.5 points; the NSE 0.767 is the top of its single-seed range (0.703-0.767). What it does not mean: an operational warning (verdict NOT YET: 51% warned, 50% of the warnings false; all high-flow days CAUTION), a result for rivers outside the 12 basins, or that the Daymet table is 'mis-stamped' as a product.

e2_outcome.value: Given the GEFS control-member rain forecast for the next three days (bias-corrected) as an input beside the rain to midnight, onsets warned 1/2/3 days ahead at the fixed warning level go from 52%/21%/13% to 44%/38%/37% (at the level chosen on the validation years: 48%/29%/23% to 54%/46%/52%; the shuffled-forecast control, 14%/4%/4%, is not a neutral baseline - it measures the harm of misleading slots to a network that trusts them - and the clean control, E2b's, equals the model without the forecast); median NSE from 0.76/0.38/0.26 to 0.69/0.52/0.45 (control 0.61/0.20/0.04), by the rule of report section 4.2: no clear difference, mixed and mixed; the verdict is NOT YET.
e2_outcome.text: Given the GEFS control-member rain forecast for the next three days (bias-corrected) as an input beside the rain to midnight, onsets warned 1/2/3 days ahead at the fixed warning level go from 52%/21%/13% to 44%/38%/37% (at the level chosen on the validation years: 48%/29%/23% to 54%/46%/52%; the shuffled-forecast control, 14%/4%/4%, is not a neutral baseline - it measures the harm of misleading slots to a network that trusts them - and the clean control, E2b's, equals the model without the forecast); median NSE from 0.76/0.38/0.26 to 0.69/0.52/0.45 (control 0.61/0.20/0.04), by the rule of report section 4.2: no clear difference, mixed and mixed; the verdict is NOT YET.

e2_outcome_caveat.value: At the fixed warning level (trigger 1.0, the level of every score of the ladder) the forecast adds -8.0, +16.8 and +23.9 points of onsets warned at 1, 2 and 3 days ahead against lstm_wqa (reading of the onsets by the seed rule, every single training of one above every single training of the other: clear loss, clear gain and clear gain) and -0.072, +0.148 and +0.197 of median NSE (reading of the NSE by the rule of report section 4.2: no clear difference, mixed and mixed); at the level chosen on the validation years the differences in onsets warned are +5.4, +17.0 and +28.6 points; at equal false-warning budgets (test years, any level; at most 40% of the onset warnings false) +10.0, +25.1 and +24.9 points and (at most 50% false) +12.1, +38.0 and +42.1; and the trigger-free average precision of the onset warnings goes from 0.460/0.242/0.181 to 0.525/0.473/0.447 (differences with 95% block-bootstrap intervals: 1 day: +0.065 (+0.004 to +0.128); 2 days: +0.231 (+0.157 to +0.297); 3 days: +0.267 (+0.196 to +0.330)). The 1-day difference at the fixed level (-8.0 points) is a moved operating point and is not established as a loss of skill: the forecast model's warnings are fewer and more often right (false warnings among the onset warnings 35% against 51%; CSI 0.355 against 0.337); at the level chosen on the validation years (trigger 0.90 against 1.05) it warns of 54% against 48% of the onsets (+5.4 points; false warnings 43% against 48%; CSI 0.385 against 0.336); a block bootstrap over the test days (30-day blocks) puts the fixed-level difference at -8.0 points (-15.1 to -1.8), which is borderline, and the paired sign test over onsets counts onsets as independent, which they are not (onsets cluster in storms and across basins). That the substitution networks over-trust slots that were exact in training is a hypothesis, not a finding. For it: the same networks warn of 69% of the 1-day onsets given the perfect rain, 44% given the forecast and 14% given a shuffled forecast (52% with no slots), and the networks retrained with the forecast (E2b) gain +20.6 points at 1 day with a harmless control. Against it, or not separating it from other causes: of the 130 onsets that lstm_wqa warns and the forecast model misses, 43 (33%) are missed even when the slots hold the perfect rain; the difference at the fixed level sits in onsets with little rain on the target day (220 of 611 with under 5 mm: 80% warned without the forecast, 42% with it, 62% with the perfect rain in the slots), follows the seasons (points of onsets warned, forecast model minus lstm_wqa: DJF +4.6, MAM -11.2, JJA -25.8, SON -12.5) and is found in 8 of 12 basins; and the forecast is light where the onsets are (it carries 0.69 of the AORC rain on the onset days and 0.63 on those with at least 5 mm, a conditional bias that the single bias factor does not remove) and has 36% exact zeros against 51% in the AORC rain. No experiment here isolates the cause: the alternatives are the warning level, small-rain onsets and a conditional bias of the forecast. Forward passes of the saved networks (forward_pass_tests; information only, nothing retrained): slots = (1 - w) x the perfect rain + w x the forecast, onsets warned at 1 day for w = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1: 68.9%, 65.8%, 58.6%, 50.7%, 43.7%; the first quarter of the way from the perfect rain to the forecast costs 12%/16%/16% of the drop in onsets warned at 1/2/3 days (a linear response would cost 25%), so the response is gradual, not steep at small departures from exact slots, which a reliance on exactness would predict; the forecast values below 0.5 mm set to zero: 43.2%, below 1 mm: 43.0% (at most 0.7 points of difference from the forecast at any lead). The shuffled-forecast control of E2a is not a neutral baseline: the network was trained on exact slots and collapses when the slots hold noise (14%/4%/4% against 52%/21%/13% with no slots; median NSE 0.61/0.20/0.04 against 0.76/0.38/0.26), so the comparison with it measures the harm of misleading slots to a network that trusts them, not the information of the forecast: the forecast is +30.0, +34.5 and +32.7 points above it, which says little, and the second half of the success rule (above the control) is met by a wide margin at every lead. The information test is E2b's control, trained and run on shuffled slots: it equals the model without slots (41%/15%/9% against 39%/14%/7%), and the forecast is +19.1, +35.0 and +37.3 points above it. Of the gap in onsets warned between lstm_wqa and a perfect rain forecast of the three days (lstm_wqaP warns of 67%/71%/73%) the forecast closes -53%, 34% and 40% at 1, 2 and 3 days ahead at the fixed level, and -262%, 36% and 38% of the NSE gap (a negative share: the forecast model is below lstm_wqa); against the old perfect-weather upper bound (lstm_wqf: 64%/67%/68%) it closes -64%, 37% and 43% of the onset gap beyond lstm_wqa. Retrained with the forecast as an input on the shorter satellite-era split (train 2000-2008, 4 test years with 335/540/656 onsets at 1/2/3 days ahead; its own scores, NOT comparable with the main split; its base is weaker: lstm_wqa_s warns of 39%/14%/7% against 52%/21%/13% for lstm_wqa), onsets warned go from 39%/14%/7% (no forecast) to 60%/50%/46% at the fixed level (control 41%/15%/9%, equal to the model without the forecast; perfect rain 71%/76%/78%), +20.6, +36.5 and +38.6 points, against -8.0, +16.8 and +23.9 for the substitution on the main split - the contrast mixes two splits and two bases and is not a measurement. At the level chosen on the validation years the E2b differences are +15.5, +9.1 and +18.6 points (the validation-chosen trigger of lstm_wqa_s, the model without the forecast, is 1.05/0.70/0.70 at 1/2/3 days, at 50%/80%/78% false warnings: where it is below 1 it buys onsets with false warnings, so the fixed level flatters the gain of the forecast there); the CSI differences are +0.111, +0.243 and +0.270 at the fixed level and +0.105, +0.204 and +0.195 at the chosen level; the trigger-free average precision gains +0.174, +0.300 and +0.321. The bias factors were fitted on 2000-2005, inside its training years (scalars; nothing of its validation or test years). On the plain gauge model, without the rain to midnight, the same forecast takes onsets warned from 19%/8%/6% to 31%/36%/36% (+12.8, +28.0 and +30.3 points). Ridge regression and the random forest given the same inputs (the forecast substituted in the same way) warn of 69%/59%/52% and 55%/47%/42% of the onsets at 1/2/3 days ahead at the fixed level, with a median NSE of 0.71/0.41/0.36 and 0.72/0.54/0.47 (the LSTM: 44%/38%/37%, 0.69/0.52/0.45; the forecast adds +13.6/+38.7/+39.9 and +6.9/+25.0/+29.9 points of onsets to them, -8.0/+16.8/+23.9 to the LSTM; false warnings among the onset warnings: ridge 62%/60%/61%, forest 45%/47%/49%, LSTM 35%/39%/42%: they warn of more onsets with more false warnings, a different operating point). Without a trigger (average precision of the onset warnings at 1/2/3 days: ridge 0.438/0.414/0.391, forest 0.500/0.460/0.420, LSTM 0.525/0.473/0.447) the forest minus the LSTM is -0.025, -0.013, -0.028 (intervals include 0: level with the LSTM) and ridge minus the LSTM -0.087, -0.058, -0.056 (intervals exclude 0: below the LSTM); at 1 day ahead, by the paired reading of the onsets at the fixed level: ridge, the simple model warns of more onsets; forest, the simple model warns of more onsets; by the NSE (report section 4.2): against ridge, no clear difference; against the forest, no clear difference - the gain of the forecast, in onsets and in NSE at every lead, does not need the network. Caveats that are part of the result: control member only (no ensemble); 0.25 degree boxes over basins of 113 to 1,928 km2; the bias factor (one per basin and lead, median 0.99) was fitted on the validation years 2000-2005, is noisy (fitted on the two halves of those years the factors differ by a median 10%/12%/14% at 1/2/3 days) and leaves a seasonal bias (mean ratio forecast / AORC at 1 day: 1.12 in summer, 0.88 in winter) and a conditional one (the corrected forecast carries 0.71/0.66/0.62 of the AORC rain on days with at least 5 mm at 1/2/3 days); raw and corrected forecasts give nearly the same onsets (-1.0, -0.4 and +0.1 points, corrected minus raw), so the correction is not what carries the result; the substitution networks never saw a forecast in training; the rain to midnight of the base rung is the AORC analysis, made after the fact (corrections about 10 days after the hour; hours before 2002 are disaggregated daily totals), not rain that could be read at midnight - the independent review of E1b tested the hindsight risk on 78 test-year days (coefficient of the pre-midnight AORC rain on the later Stage IV rain about -0.03, 95% interval -0.06 to -0.001: nothing positive) and found that with Stage IV, a real-time product, in its place for the issue day the three networks of seeds 0-2 that it tested warned of 86 to 95 of the 171 onsets of those days against 92 with AORC; the other 440 of the 611 onsets were not tested (numbers as the review's verdict states them: results/review_aorc_rain_to_midnight.json); in Eastern summer the last files of the run (from forecast hour 39 on) are posted up to 15 minutes after the issue time (results/gefs_basins.json, realtime_margin), and that margin rests on the posting times of the OPERATIONAL control member on 4 days of October 2026 (results/data_access.json), not on a long record and not on the reforecast archive, which is not an operational archive (its skill is an estimate of the operational skill, to be checked on a few months of operational GEFS before any real-time claim); five trainings per set of this script (three for the stored controls lstm_wq and lstm_wqf), so the single-training ranges are the only repetition; with five the NSE of lstm_wqaF_sub against lstm_wqa at 2 and 3 days is still 'mixed' (higher in 8 and 9 of 12 basins, Wilcoxon p = 0.176 and 0.092).

Caveats that are part of the result: control member only (no ensemble); 0.25 degree boxes over basins of 113 to 1,928 km2; the bias factor (one per basin and lead, median 0.99) was fitted on the validation years 2000-2005, is noisy (fitted on the two halves of those years the factors differ by a median 10%/12%/14% at 1/2/3 days) and leaves a seasonal bias (mean ratio forecast / AORC at 1 day: 1.12 in summer, 0.88 in winter) and a conditional one (the corrected forecast carries 0.71/0.66/0.62 of the AORC rain on days with at least 5 mm at 1/2/3 days); raw and corrected forecasts give nearly the same onsets (-1.0, -0.4 and +0.1 points, corrected minus raw), so the correction is not what carries the result; the substitution networks never saw a forecast in training; the rain to midnight of the base rung is the AORC analysis, made after the fact (corrections about 10 days after the hour; hours before 2002 are disaggregated daily totals), not rain that could be read at midnight - the independent review of E1b tested the hindsight risk on 78 test-year days (coefficient of the pre-midnight AORC rain on the later Stage IV rain about -0.03, 95% interval -0.06 to -0.001: nothing positive) and found that with Stage IV, a real-time product, in its place for the issue day the three networks of seeds 0-2 that it tested warned of 86 to 95 of the 171 onsets of those days against 92 with AORC; the other 440 of the 611 onsets were not tested (numbers as the review's verdict states them: results/review_aorc_rain_to_midnight.json); in Eastern summer the last files of the run (from forecast hour 39 on) are posted up to 15 minutes after the issue time (results/gefs_basins.json, realtime_margin), and that margin rests on the posting times of the OPERATIONAL control member on 4 days of October 2026 (results/data_access.json), not on a long record and not on the reforecast archive, which is not an operational archive (its skill is an estimate of the operational skill, to be checked on a few months of operational GEFS before any real-time claim); five trainings per set of this script (three for the stored controls lstm_wq and lstm_wqf), so the single-training ranges are the only repetition; with five the NSE of lstm_wqaF_sub against lstm_wqa at 2 and 3 days is still 'mixed' (higher in 8 and 9 of 12 basins, Wilcoxon p = 0.176 and 0.092).

e3_outcome_caveat.value: With the river gauge, 1 day ahead (lowest to highest single training in brackets): median NSE 0.590 (0.542 to 0.598) with the 12 rivers in training, 0.609 (0.581 to 0.603) with 63: no clear difference for NSE (every single seed above every single seed of the reference: no; higher in 10 of 12 rivers, p = 0.007). Onsets warned 18.7% (18.0% to 18.5%) -> 16.2% (11.9% to 17.2%) at the fixed high-flow level: hits 114 -> 99, false alarms 164 -> 101, CSI 0.147 -> 0.139; 11 onsets only the 63-river model warns of and 26 only the 12-river model: exact McNemar p = 0.020; the seed rule flags a clear loss in the share of onsets warned (every single seed of the 63-river model below every single seed of the 12-river model); the paired onsets differ (fewer onsets warned and fewer false alarms; CSI 0.147 -> 0.139); at the warning level chosen on the validation years (a multiple of the high-flow level: 0.90 against 1.00) 132 onsets (21.6%) against 114 (18.7%), false alarms 195 against 164, CSI 0.164 against 0.147; on all high-flow days at the fixed level CSI 0.508 against 0.480 (better) and false share 27% against 32%. Without the gauge: NSE 0.443 (0.355 to 0.434) against 0.458 (0.411 to 0.477): no clear difference for NSE (every single seed above every single seed of the reference: no; higher in 8 of 12 rivers, p = 0.042); onsets warned 17.2% (16.2% to 19.5%) -> 18.5% (17.0% to 20.0%) at the fixed high-flow level: hits 105 -> 113, false alarms 496 -> 440, CSI 0.095 -> 0.108; 20 onsets only the 63-river model warns of and 12 only the 12-river model: exact McNemar p = 0.215; the seed rule finds no clear difference and the paired onsets do not differ. Against the 05 numbers the seed rule reads clear gain with properties (p = 0.007; every 50-river seed above the single 05 training: yes) and clear gain without (p < 0.001; every 50-river seed above the single 05 training: yes); but each single 50-river training is +0.127, +0.161, +0.144, +0.112, +0.158 above the 05 number with properties (higher in 10, 10, 8, 11, 9 of 12 rivers; Wilcoxon p = 0.052, 0.092, 0.077, 0.027, 0.034) and +0.116, +0.095, +0.119, +0.099, +0.117 without (p = 0.001, 0.034, 0.001, 0.002, 0.001). Averaging five seeds adds 0.017 to 0.031 NSE to a single 50-river training, and the 05 numbers are single trainings. For scale, the same rivers when in training score 0.443 with the 12-river model (a seed average; its seed 0, the in-training partner of 05_lobo.py, scores 0.434, the best of its three seeds), 0.383 without properties (one training) and 0.458 with the 63-river model. No. On the validation years it is less accurate than the LSTM by 0.056 NSE in the median over the basins (single seeds do not overlap; in the mean over the basins the difference is -0.014); in the test years the difference is +0.000 NSE, within seed noise. So it is at best as accurate as the LSTM, and it needs 10.4 times the training time. This holds for this problem size - 12 basins, 20 training years, sequences of 365 days, small networks on a laptop CPU, with only the learning rate checked for each model; with 2 seeds per model the noise estimate is rough. It is not a general verdict on Transformers.

clock_what.value:
When did the rain of each flood onset fall, relative to the forecast issue time? No model is trained here.

For each flood onset of the test years (results/flood_events.csv, written by 06_flood_analysis.py) the rain of the 63 hours around the
forecast - from 09:00 of the day before the issue day t to midnight of the target day t+1 - is split by when it fell, using the cached hourly ERA5 rain at the basin centroid
(data/hourly/era5_*.json, written by check_day_windows.py). Windows, in local STANDARD time (the clocks measured in results/day_windows.json;
15_rain_to_midnight.py, which builds the input itself, uses the wall clock of the gauge):
  table   : 09:00 (t-1) -> 09:00 (t)   roughly what the Daymet rain table holds for day t: known at the issue time
  hidden  : 09:00 (t)   -> 24:00 (t)   fallen before the issue time but filed under day t+1: the model cannot see it (what E1 reveals)
  future1 : 00:00 (t+1) -> 09:00 (t+1) falls after the issue time, still inside the Daymet day t+1
  future2 : 09:00 (t+1) -> 24:00 (t+1) falls later on the target day (Daymet day t+2)
Writes results/onset_rain_clock.json and results/onset_rain_clock.csv (one row per onset). About 3 seconds.
Written 2026-10-07 by the session lead (Claude) as a diagnostic for ROADMAP.md.

unc_how_to_read.value: An interval is the range in which the number stays when the test years and the basins are drawn again: 4,000 times, 9 water years are drawn from the 9 test water years and 12 basins from the 12 basins, with replacement, and the interval runs from the 2.5th to the 97.5th percentile of the results (95 of 100 of them lie inside it). With only 12 basins and 9 year-blocks the intervals are wide; they show how much a number depends on which years and which basins it was measured on, and they are not a proof. They say nothing about rivers of another kind, about another region or about years unlike these 9, and they do not contain the difference between two trainings of the same network.

rev_aorc_rain_to_midnight_verdict.value: E1b holds up under independent recomputation, and the hindsight risk I was asked to test hard does not show up in the test years. Every number I could recompute equals the builder's (313 of 611 onsets = 51.2%, single trainings 48.6, 48.6 and 55.3%; controls 17.7, 37.5 and 18.7%; ERA5 30.0%; ridge 55.2%, forest 48.0%; replaced table 51.6%; median NSE 0.767 against 0.590; over 3,000 derived values; the 12 saved networks bit for bit from tables I built myself; the figure to 0.2 point), no hour after a window's end enters any input (90 perturbation cases), the AORC series equals my own reduction of the raw chunks (0.00 mm; 408 filled and 264 partial hours re-read from the raw files), and the engine files changed by another agent are additive and pass their test. On hindsight: the documentation shows that the channel exists by construction (daily totals on a 12 UTC gauge day spread over the hours by Stage IV's hourly shape, so an hour before midnight can carry a factor set by a day that includes rain after the issue time), but on 78 test-year days (the builder's 50 plus 28 I chose by onsets and night storms, which hold 11.8 mm of Stage IV rain after midnight on average against 1.1 mm in the builder's) the AORC rain before midnight does not depend on the Stage IV rain after it (coefficient -0.030, 95% -0.060 to -0.001; 35 dry-before/wet-after basin-days hold 0.08 mm before midnight), and the saved networks given Stage IV, a real-time product, in place of AORC for the issue day warn of 86 to 95 of the 171 onsets of those days against 92 with AORC (the rain table alone: 15). Best estimate of the part of the 51% that could be hindsight: none; at most about 3 points, measured on 28% of the onsets, not proven for the other 440 (about 10-13 GB of Stage IV would cover them). What needs fixing is wording and records, not numbers: the last clause of outcome_full ('the mis-stamped table itself costs skill') is not supported as worded, and the sentence that documents must quote says nothing about AORC being a retrospective analysis; the other items (the NSE-only reading of 'the LSTM is clearly ahead', leads 2-3, the by-period reading, the 88 GB, the log, the reproduction path, the registry announcement) are in should_fix. The 51% is a good measurement of what well-measured rain up to midnight is worth; it is not an operational warning (verdict NOT YET), and its transfer to a real-time service rests on the 171 onsets I could test with Stage IV, not yet on all 611.

rev_documents_2026_10_08_verdict.value: The numbers hold up under independent recomputation, and the four items that the documents attribute to the final critic agent are supported. All 69 sampled numbers of the documents equal the results files (c1); the headline scores of 14 prediction sets equal flood.evaluate in all 378 numbers (c2); the 24 resampling statistics that I redrew (the ranges the documents quote and verdict shares) are reproduced by 4,000 draws of my own within 0.5 point (0.0017 NSE, 0.4 point for the verdict shares) and their point estimates exactly (c3); the real-time check on all 611 onsets is reproduced from the stored Stage IV hours and the saved networks (294 / 275 / 255 onsets, 90% of the AORC effect, the 12-basin false-warning tally, the second set of networks, the controls; 161 numbers equal, c4-c7c), the rain clock from the ERA5 cache (121 fields and 611 rows equal, c8-c9), and the key figure's 1792 comparisons all agree (c10-c15). I found no numerical discrepancy and no failed check. I found two wording points while recomputing: the rain clock spans 63 hours, not 48 (S14), and 'the verdict NOT YET for onsets holds in every draw' is true for the LSTM with the river gauge and with the rain up to the evening but not for the AORC and forecast sets, where CAUTION appears in 8% and 14% of the draws at 1 day (S15). The document pass of 10:23-12:30 found eight must-fix wording items (M1-M8) and thirteen should-fix items (S1-S13); S14 and S15 were found while recomputing and S16 and S17 in the first look at the rebuilt files. Round 2 on the final files (13:48-13:50 builds): all eight must-fix items are closed; of the 17 should-fix items 12 are closed, 2 partly (S3, S15) and 3 open (S2, S13, S16), all wording or layout, none changing a number or a verdict (round_2). What this record does not establish: that the stored Stage IV hours are what a service would have had at midnight, anything about the raw Stage IV archive, or that networks trained on Stage IV would behave as those trained on AORC (see not_checked). It is one AI agent's recomputation; the team's own checks are still open.

rev_forecast_input_verdict.value: E2 holds up under independent recomputation, and I found no way for information from after the issue time to reach the forecast columns. Every number I could recompute equals the builder's (about 6,000 compared values; the 30 saved networks bit for bit from tables I built myself; 3 raw archive days decoded with my own code equal the stored box in all 268,710 values; the figure to 0.3 point; a sandbox --rescore regenerates the JSON, the figure and 189 prediction sets identically). The results: the 2- and 3-day gains of the forecast over the model without it are real and large (+18.2 and +25.3 points of onsets warned, every single training above every single training, 7 and 9 of 9 test years, intervals above zero by a block bootstrap; the retrained E2b model gains +35 and +36 points with a control that is harmless, ridge and the forest gain as much), though the median-NSE gains at those leads are 'mixed' by the project's own rule and nothing reaches GO for onsets. The 1-day 'clear loss' (-6.7 points) is a statement about one warning level, not about skill: at the level chosen on the validation years the substituted model warns of +2.6 points more with fewer false warnings, at equal false-warning budgets of +9 to +11 points, and its trigger-free average precision rises (+0.065); the over-trust explanation is only partly supported and is not isolated. Two must-fix items concern what is said, not what is computed: the lead-1 reading and two ROADMAP.md statements (the Brier skill 'same as the published numbers', the shuffled control 'shows the information is real'); twelve should-fix items follow. The E2a shuffled control measures the harm of misleading slots, not the information of the forecast; E2b's control does the latter and is clean. The E2b 1-day result (+20.3 points, +0.184 average precision, 4 of 4 test years) is a clear gain within a small split (335 onsets, 4 test years, a weaker base) and not comparable in level with E2a.

rev_more_basins_verdict.value: The numbers, the data, the engine change and the saved networks of E3 hold up under independent recomputation; I found no leakage and no arithmetic error. Every headline number of results/more_basins.json (five new sets, seven controls, three leads, and the 20 seed and average files) was reproduced with my own code to 0.0, also by flood.evaluate; the seed averages are bitwise means of their seed files, obs are the project's flow bit for bit, the stored sets hold exactly the 12. The engine change is confined to basins() and load_data(): with no ids the hand-in engine and the present engine rebuild the same 9,543,479-byte cache from the raw files, equal to the stored one; thresholds and the lstm_wq headline (median NSE 0.5896, 18.66% of onsets) are unchanged; no other script passes ids; test_flood.py passes and its new check fails for all eight deliberately broken load_data() variants. The 63 basins are exactly what the audit rule gives (recomputed from the raw files for all 78 candidates), their cache equals tables I rebuilt bit for bit, and the 12 inside it equal the stored 12. All 15 saved networks reproduce their stored forecasts bit for bit from the file alone (also with my own input matrix); their scalers equal my recomputation from the training years of the training rivers; early stopping used the validation years of the 63 (of the 50, never the 12, for the never-seen models). The never-seen training never reads the 12 (fit with the 12 absent from the dictionary gives identical weights); the nested gauge 03471500 lies 100% inside 03473000 and is the only overlapping pair of the 63. The interim scoring pass did not influence the equal-training arm: the 15-training plan is the first line of the log, the killed run printed the arm's curve and the rerun the same numbers, and the other four sets' results are unchanged. The gain rule, its words and all verdicts reproduce exactly. What the experiment shows is smaller than its sentences, and three statements say more than the data. (1) With the gauge, 63 rivers give no clear NSE gain at 1 day (0.590 -> 0.604, inside the 12-river seed range), a clear one at 2 and 3 days (+0.022, +0.028) and much steadier trainings; the onsets are not 'a clear loss': at the fixed level the model warns of 8 fewer onsets and 59 fewer false alarms with the same CSI (McNemar p = 0.24), at the level chosen on validation it warns of more (21.6% against 18.7%); the verdict stays NOT YET (must-fix 1). (2) The 'equal training' arm is not equal at the kept network: its checkpoints are the same early ones as the 1x arm (593 sequences per river against 1689 for the control), because the 63-river validation score peaks at 1000-1500 updates; it shows that a longer patience window does not move the optimum. (3) For rivers never seen, 50 training rivers give +0.16 (with properties) and +0.12 (weather only) NSE over the 05 numbers in every seed, and that survives the seed-average and budget differences; but it compares a three-seed average of one model with single trainings (a single seed's p is 0.05-0.09 with properties), and it cannot be attributed to the number of rivers: it does not rank with the distance to the nearest training gauge (rho -0.36, p 0.26) and the 50-river networks do not score lower on 27 never-seen rivers the farther they lie (rho +0.09), yet the two designs differ in number, variety and neighbours at once; the test that would separate scale from proximity (buffered leave-out, dose-response) needs training and was not done. Open before E3 can enter the report: must-fix 1 and 2 and the wording items of should-fix 1 to 5; the outcome sentence is fair arithmetic but must not be quoted without a corrected outcome_caveat.

rev_rain_to_midnight_verdict.value: The code, the numbers, the clock and the saved networks of E1 hold up under independent recomputation; I found no leakage and no arithmetic error. Every headline number of results/rain_to_midnight.json was reproduced with my own code (0.0 deviation against the engine; my own pooled onset counts give 183 of 611 for rain to midnight and 114 of 611 for the rain table alone); the three-seed files are exact means of their seeds; my independently rebuilt daily series (summer time by zoneinfo and by a hand-written rule, equal at all 298296 hours) reproduces the stored forecasts of all 12 saved networks bit for bit; no hour after local midnight of day t enters day t, also when tested through the saved networks; scalers, thresholds and early stopping use the training and validation years only; the figure shows the JSON's numbers to within a pixel; flood.py is byte-identical to the hand-in copy and test_flood.py passes. What the experiment shows is smaller than its sentence suggests. Rain up to midnight lifts the share of onsets warned 1 day ahead from 19% to 30% (control 21%, verdict NOT YET), but the NLDAS evening rain gave exactly the same 183 hits, one of the three trainings is at 27.5%, and the control is not flat, so the work order's success criterion (clearly above 30% in every seed, control flat) is NOT met with the river gauge; without the gauge the three trainings are above 30% and the control is flat, but NLDAS already scores 31.6% there, so the extra hours add nothing the evening rain had not. The outcome sentence is fair arithmetic but must not be quoted without those facts. About 8.5 of the 11 points come from the rain of day t itself and about 3 from having a second rain product. One premise rests on documentation rather than proof, that Open-Meteo stamps the END of the hour; the data lean the same way and flipping it would change the result by at most 1.3 points. Open before E1 can enter the report: the ridge/random-forest yardstick, the resampling ranges and a matched-window control.

sat_finding_read_first_gains_1_day_ahead.value: Satellite rain, soil wetness and precipitable water of the issue day are UTC-day values: their day ends at 19:00 local standard time. The gauge-based rain of the issue day ends earlier: it matches satellite rain of the UTC day before (0.55) as well as of the same UTC day (0.59; median correlations). The UTC-day inputs therefore already hold rain that the gauge table books on the next day (correlation with next-day gauge rain: gauge-based rain (Daymet) itself 0.26; satellite rain (IMERG) 0.55; day-to-day change of top-layer soil wetness (MERRA-2) 0.49; precipitable water (MERRA-2) 0.30). A gain 1 day ahead can come from this later time stamp alone: it does not show that satellite rain is more accurate than rain gauges, or that soil storage or moisture in the air adds skill (see notes).

e4a_outcome.value: At the warning level the project chose on the validation years (best CSI), the LSTM with AORC rain to midnight (an analysis made after the fact) warns of 48% of the 611 onsets 1 day ahead (hindsight at most about 4 points) with 48% of its warnings false; at the level that keeps the false share at or below 30% on the validation years it warns of 26% (test false share 32%); the perfect-rain model keeps 60% and the perfect-weather model 61% (both an upper bound that cannot be had in practice); the GO rule for the onsets (at least 70% of the onsets warned and at most 30% of the onset warnings false) is met only by the perfect weather model 2 days ahead, and there only by the seed-mean set (no single training meets it); that model is an upper bound that cannot be had in practice, and no model whose inputs can be had in practice meets it; on all high-flow days, most of them continuing floods that persistence also catches, it is met by the model with the AORC rain to midnight 1 day ahead at its CSI trigger (72% warned, 28% false) and the model with the GEFS forecast (substituted) 1 day ahead at its CSI trigger (78% warned, 26% false); a decision layer re-arranges the trade-off and does not create skill.

e4b_outcome.value: Given the rain of the last 3, 6 and 12 hours of the issue day, its wettest hour (basin mean and wettest 1 km cell) and its number of wet hours (hourly AORC rain, an analysis made after the fact) as six extra inputs beside the AORC rain to midnight to the LSTM with the river gauge, onsets warned 1 day ahead go from 52% with the AORC rain to midnight alone (hindsight at most about 4 points) to 56% (single trainings 50% to 58%; the onsets of one storm are not independent): +3.9 points over that model (340 against 316 hits of 611) and +2.9 points over the control with the same six columns one day older (53%); the share of false warnings among the onset warnings is 50% against 51% (the control: 56%); the median NSE goes from 0.76 to 0.77 (the seed-averaged forecast; single trainings 0.69 to 0.77); the verdict of results/flood_analysis.json is NOT YET for the onsets and CAUTION for all high-flow days.

e4b_outcome_caveat.value: The success rule fixed before training (wqaW above wqa and above wqaW_older in every seed at lead 1) is not met: the five single trainings with the within-day columns span 50.2% to 58.3% against 48.6% to 55.3% with the AORC rain to midnight alone and 48.8% to 53.8% for the older control; the control is flat on onsets warned (53% against 52%) and noisier (56% false against 51%; median NSE 0.74 against 0.76); 64 onsets are warned only with the within-day columns against 40 only without them. The Q95-relative flow alone (wqaQ) gives 52% (single trainings 49% to 55%) with a lower median NSE (0.73 against 0.76) and 53% false warnings (against 51%). In the 220 onsets with under 5 mm of AORC rain on the target day the share warned goes from 80% to 72% (older control 81%), in the 391 others from 36% to 47%: the gain sits in the wetter onsets, the opposite of the expectation of NEXT_EXPERIMENTS_2026-10-28.md. The gap in onsets warned from the AORC rain to midnight (52%) to the perfect rain forecast in the slots (wqaP, 67%, an upper bound that cannot be had in practice) is 15.2 points; the six columns move the share by +3.9 points and close 26% of it; in median NSE the gap is 0.028 and the move +0.006 (23% of it). At the warning level chosen on the validation years for onsets (0.95 against 1.05) wqaW warns of 60% with 53% false against 48% with 48% false; at the 30%-false operating point (the trigger chosen on the validation years so that at most 30% of the onset warnings are false: 1.50) it warns of 31% with 30% false on the test years, against 26% with 32% false for the AORC rain to midnight alone (trigger 1.55) and 30% with 31% false for the older control (trigger 1.45): at this operating point the six columns add nothing over the control. AORC is an analysis made after the fact: the within-day columns share the hindsight channel of the AORC rain to midnight (one factor per gauge day); the bound of that caveat (hindsight at most about 4 points) was measured for the daily total, not for these columns; they are a bound on what a real-time hourly rain product could add, not a service. The networks learned the within-day columns on hours that are daily totals spread by older products (all training years, 1980 to 2000, lie before 2002) and were scored on Stage IV-shaped hours; what this does to the gain was not measured. Every number of the new sets is a five-seed number; the stored sets have five seeds. With the substituted GEFS forecast beside them (wqaWF_sub against the stored wqaF_sub) onsets warned 1 day ahead go from 44% to 42% (single trainings 37% to 49%; false 33% against 35%; median NSE 0.72 against 0.69; 34 onsets warned only with the within-day columns against 47 only without them), at 2 and 3 days from 38% to 33% (15 onsets warned only with the within-day columns against 64 only without them) and from 37% to 34% (21 onsets warned only with the within-day columns against 56 only without them): by the seed rule 'no clear difference' at every lead; by the paired counts the within-day columns cost onsets at 2 and 3 days.

e4e_outcome.value: Given the state of the river at the issue time from the gauge's own 15-minute record reduced to hours (the flow at local midnight relative to Q95, its change over the last 6 and 12 hours, the day's highest hourly flow and the hours above Q95) as five extra inputs beside the AORC rain to midnight to the LSTM with the river gauge, on the satellite-era split (train 2000-10-01..2008-09-30, validation 2008-10-01..2010-09-30, test 2010-10-01..2014-09-30; flood thresholds from its training years; its numbers are comparable only inside it), onsets warned 1 day ahead go from 39% with the AORC rain to midnight alone (lstm_wqa_s, stored) to 47% (single trainings 46% to 48%; the onsets of one storm are not independent): +8.4 points (159 against 131 hits of 335); with the last available hour ending 22:00 instead of 24:00, 43% (single trainings 40% to 46%); the share of false warnings among the onset warnings is 38% against 55%; the median NSE goes from 0.71 to 0.80 (the seed-averaged forecast; single trainings 0.77 to 0.81); the verdict of results/flood_analysis.json at trigger 1.0 is NOT YET for the onsets and GO for all high-flow days.

e4e_outcome_caveat.value: The success rule fixed before training (wqaH_s above wqa_s in every seed at lead 1 on this split) is not met with the five seeds and would be with the first three (seeds 0, 1, 2): the verdict depends on the seed count (five seeds were chosen at launch with --seeds 5, the script's default being three, in one training pass before any test score was seen): the five single trainings with the river's state span 45.7% to 48.4% against 31.9% to 46.9% without it (seeds 3, 4 of wqaH_s are not above the best wqa_s seed); 45 onsets are warned only with it against 17 only without it. With the six within-day AORC rain columns beside it (wqaWH_s) 59% (single trainings 56% to 61%); with the GEFS forecast as well (wqaWHF_s against the stored lstm_wqaF_s) 1-day onsets warned go from 60% to 68% (single trainings 62% to 74% against 57% to 65%: no clear difference by the seed rule, so the +8.7 points rest on the seed-averaged forecast and on the paired onsets: 53 warned only with the new columns against 24 only without, sign test p = 0.001, a description only; false 39% against 49%), at 2 and 3 days from 50% to 48% and from 46% to 45%. Delivery: with the record ending 22:00 instead of 24:00, onsets warned 1 day ahead are 4.8 points below the 24:00 variant in the river-only sets, 2.1 points below with the within-day rain and 1.8 points above with the forecast as well, all inside the seed spread at every lead (no family separates its 24:00 and 22:00 variants seed by seed at any lead). The five columns close 26% of the gap in onsets warned from wqa_s (39%) to the perfect rain forecast in the slots (wqaP_s, 71%, an upper bound that cannot be had in practice) and 86% of the gap in median NSE. At the 30%-false operating point (the trigger chosen on the validation years so that at most 30% of the onset warnings are false: 1.20) wqaH_s warns of 38% with 25% false on the test years, against 15% with 30% false for wqa_s (trigger 1.45). The hourly record has gaps: on 1786 of the 64644 basin-days (768 in the test years) the five columns fall back to the daily mean (hourly_known = 0); the hourly flow is the gauge's own record, an input a real-time service has as provisional values and after a delivery delay (the 24:00 variant assumes none and the 22:00 variant two hours; this study used the approved record), while the AORC rain to midnight is an analysis made after the fact (hindsight at most about 4 points, a bound measured for the daily total only); the within-day columns of wqaWH_s and wqaWHF_s have no such measurement. Every number of the new sets is a five-seed number; the stored sets have five seeds; the split has 335 test-year onsets and its base is weaker than the main-split wqa.
